properties.areaDesc: East Turnagain Arm; Portage; Interior Kenai Peninsula; Turnagain Pass
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 20 at 3:55AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
Light to moderate snow will continue through late this morning
before tapering off to scattered snow showers this afternoon. Up
to three inches of additional snow accumulation is possible with
the highest amounts likely at the top of Turnagain Pass.
Visibility may be reduced to less than one mile in any heavier
snow.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
traveling. For the latest road conditions call 5 1 1 or visit
511.alaska.gov.

NWSheadline: SNOW TO CONTINUE ALONG THE SEWARD HIGHWAY FROM EASTERN TURNAGAIN ARM AND PORTAGE SOUTH TO TERN LAKE THROUGH LATE THIS MORNING

properties.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued October 20 at 6:54AM CDT until October 20 at 9:00AM CDT by NWS Milwaukee/Sullivan WI
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dense fog will reduce visibility to 1/4 to 1/2 NM.

* WHERE...Nearshore Waters from Sheboygan to North Point
Lighthouse, and Nearshore Waters from North Point Lighthouse
to Wind Point.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM CDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Low visibility will make navigation difficult.
properties.instruction:
If you must navigate, proceed with caution. Use proper fog
signals. Make sure all running lights are on. Remember to use
your radar and compass.

NWSheadline: DENSE FOG ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 9 AM CDT THIS MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Georgetown
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 20 at 7:50AM EDT until October 20 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Strong north to south longshore current. There is also a
Moderate Risk of rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Georgetown County.

* WHEN...Today.

* IMPACTS...Longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers
into rip currents, piers, jetties, and other hazardous areas.
It may sweep swimmers off their feet, making it difficult to
return to shore.
properties.instruction:
Caution should be used when in or near the water. Check with
lifeguards before entering the ocean for possible hazards you may
be swept into.

NWSheadline: BEACH HAZARDS STATEMENT REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Coastal New Hanover
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 20 at 7:50AM EDT until October 20 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents. A strong north to south longshore
current is also expected.

* WHERE...Coastal New Hanover County.

* WHEN...Today.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH THIS EVENING... ...HIGH SURF ADVISORY WILL EXPIRE AT 8 AM EDT THIS MORNING

* At 331 AM AKDT, satellite imagery indicated a strong thunderstorm,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Lone Island, Graves Harbor, Inian Island, Cape Spencer, Elfin Cove,
Three Hill Island, Palma Bay, Port Althorp, Yakobi Rock, Muir
Point, Tarr Inlet, Lemesurier Island, Surge Bay, Point Gustavus,

properties.instruction:
Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until these storms pass.

These thunderstorms will likely produce winds to around 30 knots, and
could pose a serious hazard for boaters. A Special Marine Warning may
eventually be required when these storms reach the nearshore waters.
Boaters should consider heading for shore before the storm arrives.

properties.areaDesc: Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 20 at 3:18AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A strong storm system is moving into the northern half of the Alaska
Panhandle and the northeast Gulf Coast this morning and will
continue through today. Total rain accumulation are expected to be
between 1.5-3.5 inches, with the heaviest rain late Tuesday morning
into Tuesday afternoon. Wet snow is possibly on the Klondike Highway
near White Pass up to 3 inches through tonight, though warm surface
temperatures may hinder these snow totals.

NWSheadline: HEAVY RAIN EXPECTED MONDAY NIGHT THROUGH TUESDAY

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Wind Warning, south winds 30 to 40 mph with
gusts up to 65 mph. For the Wind Advisory, south winds 20 to 30 mph
with gusts up to 50 mph expected.

* WHERE...Municipality of Skagway.

* WHEN...For the High Wind Warning, until 10 PM AKDT this evening.
For the Wind Advisory, from 10 PM this evening to 10 AM AKDT
Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High winds will blow around unsecured objects, damage
property and cause power outages. Travel will be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will remain elevated through Tuesday
morning, with the strongest gusts peaking through midday Tuesday.
Wind gusts remain strong through Wednesday morning.
properties.instruction:
People are urged to secure vessels and loose objects that could be
blown around or damaged by the wind.

Report any damage to the National Weather Service by visiting
weather.gov/Juneau/StormReports.

Winds this strong can make travel difficult. Use extra caution.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 20 at 7:06AM EDT by NWS Grand Rapids MI
properties.description:
Fog will reduce visibilities to less than a half mile across portions
of central interior Lower Michigan, particularly west and southwest
of Saginaw Bay. Motorists should anticipate rapid fluctuations in
visibilities and allow extra time to reach their destination this
morning. Slow down and add extra distance between you and the vehicle
in front of you. Visibilities will improve by mid morning.
